claim_scope: The zUSD Tau-token wallet submit path can accept an externally signed stream-9 Tau transaction without receiving a server-side private key. Admission decodes into an immutable unverified value, constructs a verified wrapper only after exact sender, current sequence, expiration, fee, operation projection, closed-field, and BLS-signature checks, and broadcasts only the reconstructed verified payload. A deterministic Tau rejection cannot be reported as submit success.
failure_modes: the server requires or receives a private key to submit a zUSD Tau-token transfer, mint, or burn
a signed transaction for another actor, sequence, expiration, fee, or operation set is broadcast
an extra or ambiguous transaction-payload field changes meaning outside the verifier's closed schema
a boolean aliases an integer transaction coordinate
a malformed or invalid BLS signature reaches sendtx
local signing authority and an external signed payload are both selected
a signed submit payload is silently accepted during the prepare phase
the HTTP authority-material classifier rejects the safe public signed envelope
a Tau node rejection is returned to the caller as a successful submission

aaa.reason: Tests arrange exact Tau state, current sequence, token operation, fee, signer, and request phase; act through prepare and submit; then assert the complete typed HTTP result, exact sent payload, signing mode, and sendtx observation. Mutation cases assert the exact reject code and empty send list.

reject_is_noop.reason: Every payload-binding, ambiguity, wrong-phase, shape, and signature rejection is observed before sendtx with an empty fake-client send list. A node-level send rejection necessarily records one attempted payload and is separately asserted never to produce a success response.

mutations.description: accept a lower, higher, or boolean transaction sequence
accept a neighboring expiration or mismatched fee limit
broadcast a different stream-9 operation projection or sender
skip BLS verification or accept an all-zero signature
treat any sendtx response as successful

nonclaims: This is a mounted transport-admission improvement for the zUSD TauToken stream. It does not prove zUSD monetary policy, token issuance authorization, global conservation, Oracle correctness, or whole-economy settlement.
The verified Python wrapper is process-local and does not constitute cryptographic publication authority, a RISC0 proof, or an opaque cross-process capability.
The underlying Tau transaction format does not add a new explicit chain-id field in this patch; operation-bound asset identifiers and the selected Tau endpoint remain deployment assumptions.
A transport timeout after possible remote acceptance remains ambiguous. Durable reconciliation, destination idempotency, and exactly-once submission are not implemented here.
The local-signing branch remains available for direct local/test fixtures but is rejected at the mounted HTTP authority-material boundary.
No UI changes are included. Clients must use the prepare response with an external signer and submit the resulting signed payload.
M6 remains research-only, production_authority remains NONE, and this packet does not establish production readiness or safety of all value movement.
